interest: This document is an illuminating archival index that traces U.S. diplomatic, military, and naval surveillance of Japanese espionage and fifth-column networks in Singapore throughout the decade preceding the outbreak of the Pacific War. It is particularly valuable for showing how American consular officials liaised with British colonial police to investigate suspected intelligence operatives, including an American citizen (Meyer Franklin Kline) and local Japanese expatriates connected via N.Y.K. steamship lines. Furthermore, it records Allied intelligence tracking the expansion of Wang Ching-wei's collaborationist apparatus into Southeast Asia through commercial fronts like Hong Kong's Chung Woh Company.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing documents and cross-reference sheets filed under decimal classification 894.20246D concerning Japanese military, intelligence, and propaganda activities in Singapore and Malaya. Spanning the period from 1932 to 1941, the docket indexes reports submitted by U.S. consular officers in Singapore (Consuls General Lester Maynard, Wilbur Keblinger, and Kenneth S. Patton) and military and naval attachés. Key topics summarized include the surveillance of Meyer Franklin Kline, an American citizen suspected by Singapore police of serving as a Japanese secret agent; inquiries into suspicious baggage left with a prominent local Japanese resident by N.Y.K. steamship travellers; the propaganda repercussions of Sino-Japanese hostilities; and the unmasking of the Chung Woh Company of Hong Kong as a Japanese and Wang Ching-wei fifth-column intelligence network operating in Singapore and the wider South Pacific area.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers indexing records and cross-references regarding Japanese military, espionage, and propaganda activities in Singapore between 1932 and 1941.
subfiles.summary: This Form DS-46 docket sheet, compiled on October 12, 1945, inventories communications and cross-reference entries filed under subject file 894.20246D concerning Japanese military activities in Singapore. The list details six individual items (Sub Nos. 2 through 7) dated between 1932 and 1941, originating from U.S. Consuls General Maynard, Keblinger, and Patton in Singapore, as well as British military and Japanese naval attachés. The purports summarize investigations of suspected secret agents like American citizen Meyer Franklin Kline, reports of Japanese spy rings and baggage inquiries involving Japanese resident Yoshio Nishimura, communist and Japanese propaganda dynamics amid Sino-Japanese hostilities, and the exposure of the Chung Woh Company as a Wang Ching-wei fifth-column organisation.
